data.title: Meta Platforms 'Reevaluating' 2030 Net Zero Goal as AI Buildout Strains Clean Energy Supply
data.description:
07:43 PM EST, 11/19/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Meta Platforms Inc ( META ) said on Thursday it is reevaluating the 2030 timeframe for its net zero emissions goal, along with its near-term intensity targets, as demand for AI infrastructure outpaces clean energy deployment, according to its 2026 sustainability report.

The company said it is "re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones" and will share where the work lands. It said its long-term net zero ambition hasn't changed.

Meta said AI infrastructure demand has grown faster than almost anyone projected, while long interconnection queues, slow permitting, lagging transmission buildout and immature supply chains for low-carbon materials and fuels have slowed progress.

The company reported 2025 net emissions of 11.8 million metric tons of CO2 equivalent, up 45% from a year earlier, driven mainly by purchased goods and services and capital goods.

Its electricity consumption rose 35%. Meta said it continues to match 100% of its annual electricity use with clean and renewable energy and has contracted more than 30 gigawatts of clean capacity to date.

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

data.title: SOCi Launches MCP Server and Expands Integrations, Strengthening the Context Layer Behind Its Agentic Workforce
data.description:
With more than 140 integrations, from Snowflake and Salesforce to Olo, Semrush and Canva, SOCi's agentic workforce learns from, works with and extends beyond the SOCi platform

SAN DIEGO, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SOCi Inc., the leader in agentic workforce solutions for multi-location enterprises, today announced the general availability of its Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, along with an expansion of the integrations that feed its context layer. SOCi's context layer is the unified source of truth for brand knowledge, guidelines and goals that guides SOCi's agentic workforce of more than 400,000 deployed Genius Agents™. With the MCP and more than 140 integrations, that intelligence now flows in from the systems enterprises already run on and out to the places their teams already work.

The announcement moves SOCi from a platform that agents work in, to an interconnected intelligence layer that speaks to, learns from and works with a brand's most important systems.

"Agents will only ever be as smart as the context they are allowed to see," said Afif Khoury, Founder and CEO of SOCi. "SOCi's context layer already knows the brand, every location and what earns visibility in local discovery. Our integrations bring in the rest of the stack, and through the MCP, our agents and tools are available wherever our customers' teams already work."

Context in: an agentic workforce that learns from the whole stack 

SOCi's Genius Agents make better decisions when they can see more of the business. SOCi's integrations bring signals from the systems that run enterprise operations into the context layer, so agents act on what is actually happening at each location. Alongside SOCi's premier integrations with Google, Meta, Yelp, Apple and Bing, SOCi connects to:

  • Data and search systems like Snowflake, Semrush (an Adobe company) and Brave
  • CRM and customer engagement systems like Salesforce and Braze
  • Creative systems like Canva and Movable Ink
  • Restaurant and loyalty systems like Olo, PAR (including Punchh) & Ovation
  • Healthcare networks like Healthgrades, WebMD and Vitals
  • Property Management systems like Yardi, RealPage and Entrata
  • Compliance and archiving systems like Smarsh, Global Relay and ProofPoint

Context out: SOCi's intelligence wherever work happens 

SOCi's MCP server, now generally available to all SOCi customers, lets AI assistants and agent frameworks that support the Model Context Protocol call SOCi's standard platform tools, agentic tools, and reporting and insights directly, so the results become part of the context those assistants work from. A marketer can ask their AI assistant to "show me my SOCi locations" or "which locations need review responses," and the assistant calls SOCi, gets the answer and responds, without the marketer logging in to another interface. SOCi customers can also work with the same tools through Ask Genius, SOCi's agentic front door to the SOCi platform.

Access is governed by SOCi's enterprise permissions. SOCi Shield applies brand and compliance rules with approval paths for work that needs a person's judgment, and SOCi holds SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 42001 credentials.

"Context flows in, so agents are grounded in how the business actually runs," said Alo Sarv, co-founder and CTO of SOCi. "And through the MCP, SOCi's tools, agents and insights flow out to wherever our customers' teams are already working. That is what makes the workforce compound."

From software you manage to work that gets done 

Enterprise brands no longer have to choose between a platform that works and a stack that connects. SOCi's agents execute local search, social and reputation work at every location, and the context layer behind them is grounded in more of the business with every system it connects to.

To learn more about SOCi's integrations and MCP server, visit www.soci.ai.

SOCi is redefining how multi-location enterprises achieve local and AI search visibility with the world's first agentic workforce. Built specifically for distributed brands, SOCi's brand-trained agents are guided by a unified visibility engine that autonomously executes and optimizes local marketing work across AI search, GEO ecosystems, social, and reviews, ensuring every location is visible, discoverable, and growing in today's localized digital landscape. Trusted by leading brands like Ford, Ace Hardware, and Liberty Tax, and recognized by Fast Company as one of the World's Most Innovative Companies, SOCi transforms marketing from software teams manage into autonomous work executed intelligently, consistently, and at enterprise scale. data.title: US signed off on sales of nearly 900,000 AI chips to China in six months, House committee says
data.description:
* Companies sought permission to ship 3.4 million AI chips during December 2025 to May 2026

* Commerce approved 75,000 shipments for Alibaba ( BABA ) and 150,000 for Tencent ( TCTZF ), committee says

* Nvidia says it has since stopped shipping H200 chips to China

(Adds Commerce Department comment in paragraph 6)

By Alexandra Alper, Katharine Jackson and Karen Freifeld

WASHINGTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - The Trump administration approved shipments of nearly 900,000 advanced AI chips made by Nvidia and AMD for Chinese companies from December 2025 through May 2026, the House Foreign Affairs Committee said on Thursday.

The approvals for 879,000 chip shipments by the Commerce Department included 75,000 for Alibaba ( BABA ), 150,000 for Tencent ( TCTZF ), 43,000 for Baidu ( BIDU ), and 4,000 for BYD, all on the Pentagon's list of alleged Chinese military-backed companies, the committee noted.

The unusual release of chip export licensing data comes as the administration of President Donald Trump faces heightened scrutiny following news about former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which has fueled renewed calls in Washington for a tougher stance on China.

Companies had sought permission to ship over 3.4 million chips to China during the period, the documents showed. It was not immediately clear how many of the approvals resulted in actual China-bound shipments of chips, which included Nvidia's ( NVDA ) H200 and AMD's equivalent MI325X.

News surrounding Huang has turned a spotlight on instances of Nvidia AI chips being smuggled to China that went unpunished, dialing up pressure on the Trump administration to crack down on Chinese tech ​threats.

The Commerce Department said its approach to H200 licensing "is based on a rule published in the Federal Register in January 2026, which imposes significant additional national security-related requirements on license applicants in order to qualify for case-by-case consideration rather than a presumption of denial."

Chris McGuire, a former US official and expert on the US-China technology battle, said, "The fact that over 30% of the AI chips sent to China were shipped to companies that the Department of War has designated as Chinese military companies is astonishing, and calls into question whether Commerce conducted any serious national security review before approving these licenses."

Nvidia said in a statement that the approvals were "subject to strict conditions and limited volumes." It added that "despite receiving some licenses, we have since stopped shipping H200s to China."

AMD said it "complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations."

Alibaba ( BABA ), Tencent ( TCTZF ), Baidu ( BIDU ), BYD, the Commerce Department and the Chinese Embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

MOST DETAILED PUBLIC DISCLOSURE

Former President Joe Biden had restricted Chinese access to the prized chips over fears that they would supercharge China's military and erode the US lead in artificial intelligence.

But Trump in December gave the green light for Nvidia to ship its H200 chip to China, rolling back Biden-era restrictions and drawing fierce criticism from China hawks across the US political spectrum.

Despite the approvals, questions swirled as to whether the AI chips were actually reaching Chinese shores.

In May, Reuters reported the US had cleared about 10 companies to buy the H200, but that no deliveries had taken place.

In testimony before the committee in July, Commerce Department official Jeffrey Kessler said shipments had begun but there had been 'very few.' Several major Chinese internet companies had each obtained about 10,000 H200 chips, Reuters has since reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

"This is the most detailed public disclosure in the history of the Export Control Reform Act," committee Chair Brian Mast, a Republican from Florida, said upon releasing the data, referring to 2018 legislation that expanded Commerce's authority to restrict the export of sensitive technologies for national security reasons.

(Reporting by Alexandra Alper, Ryan Patrick Jones, Katharine Jackson; Additional Reporting by David Shepardson; Editing by Scott Malone, Chris Sanders and Bill Berkrot)

data.title: Blue Moon Completes its Acquisition of the Turner Copper-Gold VMS Deposit
data.description:
TORONTO, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Blue Moon Metals Inc. ( BMM ) ("Blue Moon" or the "Company") (TSXV: MOON) is pleased to announce that, further to its news release dated September 23, 2026, the Company has completed its acquisition (the "Transaction") of the Turner Copper-Gold ("Turner") deposit located in O'Brien, Oregon from Gold Coast Mining Inc. ("Gold Coast"), pursuant to the terms of a definitive agreement entered into between the parties, effective September 23, 2026 (the "Definitive Agreement"). Turner is a past producing volcanic massive sulphide deposit located near the border between Oregon and California, with a similar deposit type and associated metals to the Company's Blue Moon Mine located near Mariposa, California. The Company intends to advance development studies relating to the possible commingling of extracted material for processing at a new flotation mill at the Company's Springer complex in Nevada.

Unless otherwise indicated, all dollar amounts in this news release are expressed in United States dollars.

Pursuant to the terms and conditions of the Definitive Agreement, Blue Moon acquired Turner in consideration for:

a)

a one-time cash payment of US$4,700,000 paid to Gold Coast as of the closing (the "Closing"); and


b)

the issuance of 4,778,761 common shares in the capital of Blue Moon (the "Consideration Shares") for an aggregate value of approximately US$27 million, based on a price of US$5.65 per Consideration Share (being the 20-day VWAP prior to the Definitive Agreement), to be released to Gold Coast in four (4) equal tranches over a 12 month period beginning on April 1, 2027, subject to the occurrence of an Acceleration Event (as defined herein).

In the event (the "Acceleration Event") that the VWAP of the common shares of Blue Moon (the "Blue Moon Shares") during a twenty (20) consecutive trading day period after the release of the first tranche of the Consideration Shares, is:

a)

US$7.06 per Blue Moon Share or more, then the next tranche of Consideration Shares to be released, shall be released on the first business day of the following calendar month and any subsequent tranche(s) to be released shall be released on the date that the immediately preceding tranche would have been released if such Acceleration Event had not occurred; or


b)

US$7.63 per Blue Moon Share or more, then the next tranche of Consideration Shares to be released, shall be released on the first business day of the following calendar month, and the following tranche to be released, shall be released on the first business day of the next calendar month.

The conditions of the escrow and release of the Consideration Shares are governed by an escrow agreement entered into between Blue Moon, Gold Coast, and Odyssey Trust Company, acting as escrow agent.

The following additional milestone payments (the "Milestone Consideration") are payable to Gold Coast upon the achievement of any of the following:

a)

A cash payment in the amount of US$2,000,000 upon receiving the necessary permits to begin underground exploration and/or development of Turner;


b)

A cash payment in the amount of US$2,000,000 upon receiving the necessary permits to begin mining of Turner; and


c)

A cash payment in the amount of US$3,000,000 six months following the commencement of commercial production from Turner.

If the Milestone Consideration has not been paid in full by the sixth (6th) anniversary from the date of Closing, Blue Moon shall pay to Gold Coast, four (4) annual cash installments of US$500,000 and a final cash payment in the amount of the remaining balance of the Milestone Consideration that has not yet been paid. Blue Moon may prepay the Milestone Consideration at any time and without penalty.

Gold Coast and Blue Moon are arm's length parties and no finder's fees or commissions were payable by Blue Moon in connection with the Transaction. For further information regarding Turner, refer to the press release of Blue Moon dated September 23, 2026 filed on SEDAR+.

About Blue Moon

Blue Moon is advancing 6 brownfield polymetallic projects, including the Nussir copper-gold-silver project in Norway, the NSG copper-zinc-gold-silver project in Norway, the Blue Moon zinc-gold-silver-copper project in the United States, the Springer tungsten-molybdenum project in the United States, the Apex germanium-gallium-copper project in the United States and the Turner copper-gold-zinc-silver project in the United States. All 6 projects are well located with existing local infrastructure including roads, power and historical infrastructure. Zinc, copper and tungsten are currently on the USGS and EU list of metals critical to the global economy and national security and germanium and gallium are also on the USGS list of critical metals. data.title: Exclusive-Citi incorrectly booked trades, underestimated risky assets by $35 billion, sources say
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Citigroup ( C ) incorrectly booked trades at a European subsidiary that underestimated its risk-weighted assets, two people familiar with the matter said, in a setback for the US lender that has been trying to fix regulatory issues.  

Citigroup ( C ) underestimated risk-weighted assets by about $35 billion at a trading unit in Europe, one person familiar with the matter said.  

In a statement to Reuters, Citigroup ( C ) said the bank had identified and resolved an internal capital modeling issue at a European trading subsidiary this summer. "The subsidiary remained fully compliant with regulatory minimums throughout, with no impact on the holding company or main operating bank," the bank said. "Citi completed remedial actions and injected capital to immediately restore the subsidiary's buffers."

The Wall Street firm incorrectly recorded trades at its UK securities unit using an internal model based on its own statistical assumptions, the people said. Regulators had not approved the model for those types of transactions, they added. Once the trades were recorded using a standard risk model, the value of RWAs shot up significantly, the people said.

The mishap is a setback for Citi CEO Jane Fraser, who has been trying to get the bank out of the regulatory penalty box for years. Citi has operated under tight supervisory scrutiny and as recently as the summer was targeting submitting paperwork to regulators this year to get the restrictions lifted, Reuters has reported.

Shaking off the regulatory shackles would free up resources, become a key achievement for Fraser and bolster Citigroup ( C ) shares, according to analysts.

Citi's problems stretch back to 2020, when it was told to remediate longstanding risk management and data governance problems identified by the Fed and Office of the Comptroller of the Currency. It was fined $400 million and agreed to a long list of longstanding issues it needed to fix, but was then fined another $136 million in 2024 for the delay in fixing its data management problems.

(Reporting by Tatiana Bautzer and Elisa Martinuzzi; Editing by Paritosh Bansal, Megan Davies and John Mair)

The number of drivers picking up from airports rose by a double-digit percentage versus the prior week, the spokesperson said. Lyft ( LYFT ) raised driver bonuses to meet peak demand that evening and offered airport riders a discount code worth up to $15 through the weekend, according to the report.

data.title: Anthropic's blockbuster debut tests Wall Street's faith in AI boom
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Anthropic notched a valuation of about $2 trillion in its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, edging past SpaceX's June listing and capping a turbulent stretch for the AI sector that tested Wall Street's appetite for the technology.

The early exuberance faded, however, signaling volatility ahead as investors locked in quick gains and the main indexes retreated amid renewed jitters over the sector's outlook.

Shares of the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company opened at $111.50, which was 34% higher than the IPO price of $83 set on Wednesday. But the stock pared gains and ended the day at $97.17, up 17% from its IPO price.

Anthropic's fully diluted $2 trillion valuation includes stock options and restricted stock units that the company has promised employees but which have not been vested into actual shares. Based on Anthropic's outstanding shares, the company's value reached as much as $1.5 trillion on Thursday, on par with Tesla.

The AI market euphoria has somewhat cooled in recent weeks, with last week's resignation of Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang causing concern. The technology has boosted economic growth but has prompted unease about mounting debt loads and doomsday warnings. An anti-data-center movement may have helped Democrats sweep the US midterm elections.

"The blockbuster Anthropic launch is a critical step in reassuring the market about the potential for AI, but it's really just the beginning," said Bob O'Donnell, chief analyst at TECHnalysis Research. "We still need to see what happens with OpenAI, how the Nvidia ( NVDA ) situation evolves, how the political climate for data centers shapes up, and what the historical performance for Anthropic proves to be before we'll get any real sense of stability."

The six-year-old company has positioned itself as the gatekeeper of AI safety while selling investors the idea that it can be profitable despite massive compute costs. Led by Dario Amodei, a former OpenAI employee, Anthropic has also signaled it may tap debt markets.

"At some point in the future we're hoping to be investment grade, and debt is an instrument that we have available to us, and we'd like to use at some point in the future," CEO Amodei told CNBC in an interview on Thursday.

Anthropic's net loss narrowed in the third quarter as revenue jumped 47% from the previous quarter, even as the pace of growth slowed sharply from the prior quarter. The company has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Alphabet's Google.

INDUSTRY BENCHMARK, EMPLOYEE PAYDAY

As the first frontier AI company to go public, Anthropic is poised to become the sector's benchmark. The company sold 980 million shares at $83 each, pricing the IPO above its initial range of $70 to $78 set when it launched the road show.

Its IPO proceeds could climb to as much as $93.5 billion if underwriters fully exercise their option to purchase additional shares. Currently, the figure sits at over $107 billion, including the additional $26 billion raised through a private placement. AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia ( NVDA ) and TSMC were the investors in the private placement.

"Some of the demand may simply reflect investors not wanting to miss out on the rare opportunity to gain exposure to a leading AI company, even if its long-term profitability remains uncertain," IPOX associate Lukas Muehlbauer said.

London-based index rebalance analytics firm Intropic estimates passive demand from index-tracking funds will account for the purchase of up to 30% of Anthropic's shares offered by the end of the year.

Anthropic's IPO is set to create thousands of paper millionaires and a handful of billionaires, rewarding everyone from early researchers and engineers to administrative staff.

Based on the IPO price, Amodei and his six co-founders, who together own about 10% of the company, had stakes worth nearly $150 billion combined, according to a Reuters calculation based on details in the filing.

JUSTIFYING THE PRICE TAG

Debate has intensified over whether the AI boom is becoming a bubble as soaring valuations and a web of circular deals involving AI developers, chipmakers, cloud providers and investors fuel questions about the durability of the industry's growth.

Anthropic's breakneck growth has so far insulated it from these concerns, but some investors have said they may wait for the initial euphoria to subside before buying.

Anthropic "isn't a prudent 'buy-at-any-price' opportunity for retail wealth clients," said Talley Leger, chief market strategist at The Wealth Consulting Group. "History shows that retail investors buying hot tech IPOs on day one historically underperform broad market indexes over a 3-year horizon."

The company will also need to balance growth with calls to slow the development of advanced AI models. Anthropic warned in its IPO prospectus that AI could behave unpredictably and advance faster than oversight mechanisms.

The massive IPO will earn the underwriters, led by Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, a $550 million fee, a regulatory filing showed.

(Reporting by Niket Nishant, Manya Saini in Bengaluru and Echo Wang in New York; Additional reporting by Chibuike Oguh, Noel Randewich, Anhata Rooprai and Pritam Biswas; Editing by Christian Plumb, Arun Koyyur, Sayantani Ghosh and Matthew Lewis)

data.title: Fed's Paulson says understanding, not guidance, drives effective communication
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said on Thursday central bank communications work better when officials and the public understand one another, rather than when Fed officials provide explicit comments about what they think lies ahead.

For the Fed, "understanding matters more than the specific ways we communicate," Paulson said in the text of a speech to be delivered before a gathering held by the Money Marketeers of New York University.

"When we understand each other, we don't need to say as much when new data arrive," she said, adding, "You can anticipate how we'll respond, and we can act in ways that are steady and, for the most part, predictable."

WARSH'S COMMUNICATION OVERHAUL

Paulson's views on Fed communications come as the central bank has been overhauling how it explains its actions to the public. Under new Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, the Fed has shortened its Federal Open Market Committee policy statement and has launched a special task force to weigh how the Fed should communicate its actions and views.

At the same time, Warsh has, in contrast to other recent Fed leaders, stepped almost entirely away from providing any guidance about the interest-rate outlook.

But even as Warsh has pulled back, many of his colleagues on the central bank have continued to provide regular updates on where they think interest-rate policy is heading and how the economy is faring.

Paulson did not offer any comments about the near-term outlook for interest-rate policy, as the central bank approaches its December 8-9 Federal Open Market Committee meeting, where it is widely expected to hike rates by a quarter percentage point, to between 4% and 4.25%.

Paulson said in her remarks that understanding how the Fed reacts to incoming data is particularly important.

"Communication works best when it builds a shared understanding of the reaction function, and that credibility is essential, because people act on messages they trust," she said.

Paulson said an understanding of what the Fed is doing and why helped markets navigate the Fed's decision to hold rates steady in late October after boosting them in September and signaling more hikes were in the works.

"In October, markets expected further tightening, so the pause did not leave policy behind where it needed to be," she said. "A shared understanding of the reaction function allowed policy to move deliberately and gave people time to adjust, without the risk that a pause was mistaken for a stop."

(Reporting by Michael S. Derby in New York; Editing by Matthew Lewis)

data.title: Exclusive-Citi incorrectly booked trades, underestimated risky assets by $35 billion, sources say
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Citigroup ( C ) incorrectly booked trades at a European subsidiary that underestimated its risk-weighted assets, two people familiar with the matter said, in a setback for the US lender that has been trying to fix regulatory issues.  

Citigroup ( C ) underestimated risk-weighted assets by about $35 billion at a trading unit in Europe, one person familiar with the matter said.  

In a statement to Reuters, Citigroup ( C ) said the bank had identified and resolved an internal capital modeling issue at a European trading subsidiary this summer. "The subsidiary remained fully compliant with regulatory minimums throughout, with no impact on the holding company or main operating bank," the bank said. "Citi completed remedial actions and injected capital to immediately restore the subsidiary's buffers."

The mishap is a setback for Citi CEO Jane Fraser, who has been trying to get the bank out of the regulatory penalty box for years. Citi has operated under tight supervisory scrutiny and as recently as the summer, was targeting submitting paperwork to regulators this year to get the restrictions lifted, Reuters has reported.

(Reporting by Tatiana Bautzer and Elisa Martinuzzi; Editing by Paritosh Bansal and Megan Davies)

data.title: California AG subpoenas Nvidia over concerns about former CEO, China ties
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - California Attorney General Rob Bonta said on Thursday his office had served an investigative subpoena to Nvidia ( NVDA ) related to reports of former CEO Jensen Huang's alleged affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

"The conduct of Nvidia ( NVDA ) and its former CEO raises bright red flags," Bonta said, adding that his office was examining whether Nvidia ( NVDA ) or Huang's actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips or confidential information, and if the company misled investors and the public about the risk.

The probe will help determine whether Nvidia's ( NVDA ) actions violated California law, the attorney general's office said.

Huang resigned last week after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang and two with Nvidia ( NVDA ) employees.

US intelligence agencies are trying to determine the extent of Alice Huang's ties to China's Ministry of State Security and what information she may have passed to Beijing, according to Reuters.

China has rejected allegations of an espionage operation targeting Jensen Huang.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board has ruled out bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO, despite a campaign by employees and prominent technology figures, including Elon Musk, to reinstate him.

The US Securities and Exchange Commission is also reportedly probing Nvidia ( NVDA ) after Huang's resignation.

The House Foreign Affairs Committee said on Thursday that the Trump administration had approved shipments of nearly 900,000 advanced Nvidia ( NVDA ) and AMD AI chips to Chinese companies between December 2025 and May this year, although it was unclear how many were ultimately shipped.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) said the approvals were subject to strict conditions and limited volumes and that it had stopped shipping H200 chips to China.

(Reporting by Harshita Mary Varghese in Bengaluru; Editing by Shinjini Ganguli)

data.title: From anti-war physicist to AI power broker, Amodei takes his safety approach public
data.description:
By Aditya Soni and Jeffrey Dastin

Nov 19 (Reuters) - Long before Dario Amodei butted heads with the Pentagon over whether the US military could use Anthropic's models for mass domestic surveillance and fully autonomous weapons, he was fighting another battle.

At the California Institute of Technology in 2003, Amodei called on his classmates to join him in protesting the US invasion of Iraq, writing in an op-ed that citizen-scientists should not be "reduced to amoral technicians who run the machines of war."

On Thursday, as 43-year-old Amodei led his startup to an IPO that raised a record $81 billion and valued it at about $1.5 trillion, the listing cemented his transformation from an idealistic physics student into one of the most powerful custodians of the AI age.

"We will not bend to either business nor political pressure," Amodei said at the Nasdaq on Thursday in New York. "Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing."

Amodei has spent much of his ascent emphasizing curbs on a technology whose extraordinary potential he has devoted his career to unlocking, and has now made his company one of the most valuable on Wall Street. Even as Anthropic prepared for its debut, Amodei penned a nearly 4,000-word essay in September, warning how AI's advances could outpace human control and urging a slowdown in development.

Days later, Anthropic released a new version of one of its most powerful models in a challenge to rival OpenAI, where he worked before quitting over differences related to AI safety.

In that essay, Amodei denied any contradiction between his quest for safe AI and Anthropic's race to develop the most powerful models.

"I have grappled with this duality of risk and benefit since the beginning of Anthropic," he wrote. "Not building the technology deprives humanity of benefits or simply places AI in the hands of authoritarian powers, while building it too fast is reckless."

Anthropic was a commercially viable company spurring a safety "race to the top," he said.

This approach has drawn criticism both from advocates of greater safety measures and from Silicon Valley executives who have warned against slowing down innovation, such as Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang. Amodei's determination to impose some limits on AI also earned him enemies in Washington, culminating in an extraordinary showdown with the Trump administration early this year. 

Following a meeting between Amodei and US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, the government set a deadline for Anthropic to accept the military's contract terms, which the company rejected. That led to a government blacklist of its technology that the Claude maker challenged in court.

Anthropic declined to comment for this story. 

Anthropic shares rose sharply on their first day of trading, debuting at $111.50, 34% higher than the $83 IPO price. 

THE PRICE OF CAUTION

Though the IPO was expected to mint thousands of paper millionaires, Amodei has said the company's safety focus has come at a cost.

Last month he responded to a post on X that challenged Anthropic's safety record and criticized a change to its pledge around halting AI development if it cannot minimize risks. Amodei said the company had "likely sacrificed a significant chunk of a several-month model lead" by delaying the release of its powerful Mythos models over hacking risks and initially limiting access to cybersecurity defenders.

Anthropic is spending billions of dollars on computing capacity each year, making it harder as a publicly traded company - albeit one where its seven co-founders or a trust wield voting control on key matters - to justify slowing model development as shareholders seek returns.

In its IPO filing, though, the company noted that its corporate setup could lead to decisions that "may conflict with short-, medium-, or long-term financial interests and business performance," and said it had paused training of a next-generation ‌flagship AI model for more than a month over security concerns.

LESSONS FROM THE ATOM BOMB

Dario Amodei and his sister and co-founder Daniela grew up in San Francisco's Mission District, just a few miles from the spot where Anthropic would eventually occupy a glass tower with Silicon Valley perks such as a gourmet espresso bar.

He was voted "most likely to succeed" by his eighth-grade classmates, a yearbook snippet shows, and admitted to San Francisco's selective Lowell public high school. He went to Caltech before transferring to Stanford, and then attended Princeton, where he earned a PhD focusing on biophysics and computational neuroscience.

After his father's death from hepatitis C about two decades ago - a few years before medical advances dramatically improved survival rates - Amodei pursued artificial intelligence that could accelerate medicine. In a podcast, talking about his dad's illness, Amodei pushed back against criticism that he was simply an AI "doomer."

Amodei's preoccupation with AI safety has influenced his management style.

Daniela Amodei has oversight of day-to-day operations at the company, while Dario Amodei devotes almost 40% of his time to framing the culture and vision of Anthropic through essays and fortnightly company-wide meetings that employees have dubbed "Dario Vision Quests."

"Operationally, the buck stops with her," a former employee said of Anthropic President Daniela Amodei. "Strategically, it stops with him."

Dario Amodei said in a Bloomberg interview published in June that he had only one direct report, calling the structure "incredibly freeing."

One of his favorite books is "The Making of the Atomic Bomb," written by Richard Rhodes. Talking about Robert Oppenheimer, the bomb's architect, Amodei said: "In some ways I actually see Oppenheimer as a failure case, as what should not happen."

(Reporting by Aditya Soni in Bengaluru and Jeffrey Dastin in San Francisco; Writing by Sayantani Ghosh; Editing by David Gaffen)

data.title: RADIN Health Unveils RADINA™, the Autonomous AI Ecosystem for Imaging, at RSNA 2026
data.description:
One autonomous AI platform guiding every patient from referral to follow-up, automating repetitive work, connecting workflows, and helping imaging organizations scale without adding administrative complexity.

SHERIDAN, Wyo., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- RADIN Health today announced RADINA, a next-generation AI platform designed to automate and orchestrate imaging workflows across the entire patient journey. Scheduled to be officially unveiled at RSNA 2026, RADINA serves as the AI layer behind RADIN™, connecting operational, clinical, and patient-facing workflows into a single intelligent ecosystem.

Imaging organizations face continued pressure from workforce shortages, rising labor costs, increasing patient volumes, reimbursement cuts, and growing compliance requirements. While healthcare software has digitized many imaging processes, organizations still rely heavily on staff to coordinate referrals, insurance verification, prior authorizations, scheduling, patient communications, reporting workflows, and follow-up management.

"Healthcare doesn't need more dashboards, more queues, or more disconnected applications," said Dr. Alejandro Bugnone, Chief Executive Officer of RADIN Health. "It needs systems that understand what should happen next and can make it happen. RADINA was built to automate repetitive work, eliminate unnecessary handoffs, and help imaging organizations scale without increasing administrative complexity."

Unlike traditional workflow tools that automate individual tasks, RADINA continuously evaluates the state of each patient's journey and determines the next action required to move care forward. The platform follows patients from referral intake through scheduling, authorization, imaging, reporting, and follow-up management while escalating exceptions to staff when human judgment is required.

RADINA moves beyond traditional workflow automation by coordinating the next best action across the imaging journey and executing routine operational tasks from referral intake through follow-up. The platform was built around a simple principle: "If the system knows what has to happen next, nobody should have to remember it."

Experience the Official RADINA Launch at RSNA 2026

RSNA attendees are invited to visit RADIN Health Booth #5515 for the official launch of RADINA™ on Sunday, November 29 at 10:40 AM. Visitors will have the opportunity to meet the RADINA Concierge robot, an AI-powered digital front desk that greets patients, automates check-in, supports registration workflows, and can escort patients to their destination within an imaging center. Available as a mobile robotic assistant, self-service kiosk or tablet, RADINA Concierge demonstrates how imaging organizations can modernize patient access while reducing administrative burden and improving operational efficiency. 

RSNA 2026 attendees can also experience live demonstrations of RADINA at the RADIN Health exhibit booth #5515. Dr. Alejandro Bugnone is scheduled to speak at RSNA on Guiding the Referral-to-Follow-Up Patient Journey on November 30 from 1:00 PM to 1:20 PM at Innovation Theater, Booth 3352, and on Agentic AI with Clinical Oversight on December 1 from 12:00 PM to 12:20 PM at AI Theater, Booth 5536.

RADINA Autopilot™ - The Autonomous Imaging Workflow Engine

At the center of the platform is RADINA Autopilot™, an autonomous workflow engine that connects imaging operations into a single continuous workflow. Autopilot manages each patient's progression through the imaging process and automatically initiates the next appropriate step. It runs the entire referral-to-follow-up cycle as one workflow while engaging staff only when decisions require human oversight.

RADINA Autopilot can:

  • Process incoming referrals and orders
  • Verify insurance eligibility and medical necessity
  • Manage scheduling workflows
  • Coordinate prior authorizations
  • Engage patients through voice, chat, and digital communications
  • Send forms, perform digital check-in, and collect patient payments
  • Monitor report quality and compliance
  • Track completion of radiologist report imaging follow-up recommendations

According to RADIN Health, imaging organizations spend significant administrative time moving patients from referral to completed exam. RADINA is designed to reduce manual effort by automating routine tasks and allowing staff to focus on exceptions, patient support, and clinical coordination.

A Connected AI Ecosystem

RADINA includes AI-powered products and capabilities spanning imaging operations, radiologist productivity, quality assurance, compliance, and revenue optimization. The platform operates as a unified intelligence layer across the imaging enterprise, following the patient from referral through follow-up. 

Before the Exam

  • OCR for orders and referrals
  • Insurance verification and medical necessity validation
  • Intelligent appointment scheduling
  • Conversational patient scheduling
  • Prior authorization automation
  • Digital payment collection
  • Autonomous patient check-in

Quality, Compliance, and Revenue

  • Report quality review
  • Documentation compliance validation
  • Follow-up recommendation tracking
  • Closed-loop patient follow-up management

"RADINA represents a new generation of technology that doesn't just document work, it helps perform it," said Dipali Lohar, Chief Product Officer of RADIN Health.

The platform maintains a single workflow and timeline for every patient, enabling organizations to reduce administrative friction, minimize missed steps, improve patient engagement, and ensure follow-up recommendations are completed.

About RADIN Health

RADIN is a comprehensive cloud-native platform and intelligent workflow ecosystem for radiology and diagnostic imaging organizations. Its technology unifies enterprise imaging, RIS, PACS, SELECT workflow orchestration, dictation, intelligent worklists, clinical communications, patient engagement, analytics, compliance, and AI-powered automation within a single connected environment. Designed for hospitals, imaging centers, radiology groups, and teleradiology practices, RADIN helps healthcare organizations improve operational efficiency, clinical quality, patient access, financial performance, scalability, and care coordination across the entire imaging journey, from referral to follow-up.

For more information, visit www.radinhealth.com.

data.title: Anthropic's $1.5 trillion debut rewrites venture capital's playbook
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - For decades, venture capital thrived on small bets that became billion-dollar companies.

Then came Anthropic, rewriting the playbook and forcing investors to write fatter checks to buy stakes at unheard-of valuations. 

The AI lab's shares began trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday at a $1.5 trillion valuation, delivering multibillion-dollar windfalls to venture investors at a moment when the industry needs fresh liquidity to fund more bets on AI companies. The stock closed at $97.17, up 17% from its IPO price of $83.

Anthropic's stock market value ended the day at about $1.3 trillion, based on its outstanding shares, or $1.8 trillion, based on its fully diluted shares.

To join the fundraising frenzy, especially at later stages, venture capital firms invested billions, tapping their own investors for additional capital through special-purpose vehicles.

MENLO, SPARK REAP BIG RETURNS

Menlo Ventures and Spark Capital emerged with some of the biggest returns by multiple. Spark Capital was the first venture capital firm to lead an Anthropic investment, in a $450 million Series C round in 2023 at a valuation of $4.5 billion. Spark general partner Yasmin Razavi, who spearheaded the investment, remains the only investor who sits on Anthropic's board.

Writing the largest check in the firm's history, early-stage firm Menlo invested over $1 billion for a stake of nearly 1.5%, according to a person familiar with the investment. At a $1.5 trillion market cap, Menlo's stake is worth over $20 billion. 

To invest beyond the capacity of its existing fund, Menlo raised a $750 million special-purpose vehicle from limited partners, a tactic that became increasingly common as funding rounds grew, given the capital needs of AI companies.

THE LATE-STAGE BETS PAID OFF

Sequoia Capital, long known for its early bets, joined a later round and still stands to earn billions of dollars.

Sequoia passed on Anthropic at lower prices. After a leadership change, it wrote its first check at the start of this year, joining a round led by Singapore's GIC and Coatue at a $380 billion post-money valuation in February. It later co-led, alongside Altimeter, Dragoneer and Greenoaks, a round at $965 billion. Sequoia has invested $3 billion in Anthropic and continued to invest more through Anthropic's IPO, signaling further conviction in the AI lab. 

Lightspeed Venture Partners, which invested more than $3 billion in Anthropic, now holds over 2% of the company, making it the largest financial investor in the company, according to two people familiar with the matter. 

The returns are possible because of the rapid rise in Anthropic's valuation and revenue. Its annualized revenue grew from about $1 billion at the start of 2025 to about $81 billion last month, as its valuation climbed from $61.5 billion in March 2025 to $965 billion in the latest private round this May.

Strategic backers, too, supply much of the unprecedented capital and computing power needed by AI labs. The combined stake of Amazon and Alphabet's Google in Anthropic is about 28.4%.  

"We're living through a very unique time of profound change happening at a higher velocity than ever before. The scale of the impact of these businesses and the breadth of market opportunities is larger than anything we've seen before. And that is going to afford investment opportunities that are larger than what we've seen in the past," said Will Griffith, a partner at Iconiq, which has invested $6.1 billion, making the fund the second-largest financial investor by ownership in Anthropic. 

(Reporting by Krystal Hu in San Francisco; Additional reporting by Noel Randewich in San Francisco; Editing by Sayantani Ghosh and Matthew Lewis)

data.title: TPG to take BILL Holdings private in $6 billion deal
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Fintech firm BILL Holdings ( BILL ) said on Thursday it will be acquired by private equity group TPG, in partnership with Corpay ( CPAY ), in an all-cash transaction valued at about $6 billion.

BILL will be acquired for $63.25 per share. The offer represents a 31% premium to the 60-day volume-weighted average share price through November 16, the last full trading day before BILL takeover talks were reported.

The company was valued at a little under $5 billion before the media reports. Its shares fell about 3.7% in after-hours trading.

Corpay ( CPAY ) will invest $1.1 billion for a roughly one-third stake in the company, with an option to buy the rest.

"We expect the transaction to be accretive to Corpay ( CPAY ) cash EPS in 2027, and the take-private transaction structure gives the company the flexibility to transform and accelerate profit growth. We have the option to buy the rest of the company in 2030," said Peter Walker, CFO of Corpay ( CPAY ).

The deal is set to close in the first half of 2027.

BILL provides cloud-based software that helps small and midsize businesses automate financial operations, including accounts payable and receivable.

Investor pressure on BILL mounted in September last year after activist investor Starboard Value disclosed an 8.5% stake and nominated four board candidates, signaling a potential proxy fight.

Around the same time, Reuters reported that activist Elliott Investment Management had also built a large stake and pushed for a sale. Facing competition from newer rivals offering cheaper alternatives, BILL was exploring a sale, Reuters had reported a year ago, citing sources.

Starboard Value, BILL's largest stockholder, agreed to vote its shares in favor of the agreement, the companies said.

Analysts say the company's improved margins following its plan to cut about 30% of its workforce earlier in the year have boosted its appeal as a takeover target.

Goldman Sachs and Qatalyst Partners are financial advisors to BILL. Barclays is exclusive financial advisor to Corpay ( CPAY ).

(Reporting by Pritam Biswas in Bengaluru; Editing by Tasim Zahid and Shinjini Ganguli)

data.title: BILL Agrees to be Acquired by TPG in Partnership with Corpay
data.description:
BILL will be acquired for $63.25 per share in an all-cash transaction, representing a fully diluted equity value of approximately $6.0 billion

SAN JOSE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- BILL , the intelligent finance platform trusted by nearly 500,000 businesses to manage, move, and maximize their money, today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to be acquired by TPG, a leading global alternative asset management firm, in partnership with Corpay ( CPAY ) , the Global Spend Management Company. BILL will be acquired for $63.25 per share in a cash transaction that values BILL at $6.0 billion. TPG will acquire a majority interest in BILL through TPG Capital, the firm’s U.S. and European private equity platform, and Corpay ( CPAY ) will acquire a minority interest.

The per share purchase price represents a 31% premium to the 60-day volume-weighted average price ending on November 16, the last full trading day preceding media reports that BILL was in acquisition discussions.

“This transaction marks an exciting new chapter for BILL, delivering significant, certain, and immediate value to our stockholders, while creating new opportunities to accelerate our transformation and deliver greater value to customers,” said René Lacerte, CEO and Founder of BILL. “With our new partners, we will have the resources, expertise, and strategic support to accelerate innovation, advance our AI transformation, and continue to drive the future of financial operations. We look forward to the opportunities ahead for our customers and our business.”

“BILL has built a differentiated financial operations platform that helps small and midsize businesses manage their most critical financial workflows. We have long recognized the significant opportunity at the intersection of financial technology, AI, and payments, and believe BILL is well positioned to capitalize on these trends through its scaled network, integrated technology, and deep customer relationships,” said John Flynn, Partner at TPG. “We are excited to partner with the BILL team, combining TPG’s technology investing and business-building experience with Corpay’s payments expertise to accelerate innovation and support the company's next chapter,” added Tim Millikin, Partner at TPG.

“We’re excited about the potential this agreement represents and have great respect for everything the BILL team has accomplished. We see clear opportunities to support and complement BILL’s product roadmap, platform capabilities, and the services it offers to a broader range of customers. We look forward to working with BILL to further enhance its market-leading platform to deliver greater innovation and value to customers,” said Ron Clarke, Chairman and CEO of Corpay ( CPAY ).

Transaction Details
The transaction, which was approved unanimously by the BILL Board of Directors, is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to customary closing conditions, including approval by BILL stockholders and the receipt of required regulatory approvals. There are no financing conditions to the transaction. Starboard Value, BILL's largest stockholder, and BILL’s CEO and Founder, René Lacerte, have agreed to vote their shares in favor of the agreement.

Upon the close of the transaction, Mr. Lacerte will continue to lead BILL as CEO. BILL will become a privately held company, and its common stock will no longer be listed on any public stock exchange.

Advisors
Goldman Sachs and Qatalyst Partners are serving as financial advisors to BILL, Fenwick & West LLP is serving as BILL’s legal advisor, and Joele Frank, Wilkinson Brimmer Katcher is serving as strategic communications advisor.

BofA Securities, Inc., Deutsche Bank Securities Inc., and RBC Capital Markets, LLC are serving as financial advisors to TPG. Davis Polk & Wardwell LLP is serving as legal counsel.

Barclays is serving as financial adviser to Corpay ( CPAY ). Sullivan & Cromwell LLP is serving as legal counsel.

About BILL
BILL is the intelligent finance platform trusted by nearly half a million businesses and their accountants to manage, move, and maximize their money. BILL powers businesses ranging from fast-moving startups to growing companies with complex operations. We use AI to deliver strategic finance capabilities in one integrated platform that includes AP, AR, expenses, forecasting, procurement and more. With a member network of more than 9 million, BILL’s platform processes over 1% of US GDP annually. Headquartered in San Jose, California, BILL is a trusted partner of leading U.S. financial institutions, accounting firms, and software providers. For more information, visit bill.com.

About TPG
TPG is a leading global alternative asset management firm, founded in San Francisco in 1992, with $346 billion of assets under management and investment and operational teams around the world. TPG invests across a broadly diversified set of strategies, including private equity, impact, credit, real estate, and market solutions, and our unique strategy is driven by collaboration, innovation, and inclusion. Our teams combine deep product and sector experience with broad capabilities and expertise to develop differentiated insights and add value for our fund investors, portfolio companies, management teams, and communities.

About Corpay ( CPAY )
Corpay ( CPAY ) , the Global Spend Management Company, is an S&P 500 company with three primary B2B solution sets. Spend Management, provides corporate and virtual card programs and AP automation solutions. data.title: New Orleans passes budget with 3.4% deficit
data.description:
Key Insight: Discover how New Orleans reduced its projected 2027 general fund budget deficit.
What's at Stake: New Orleans credit ratings, already in BBB category from two agencies.
Expert Quote: "Next year won’t be any easier" — Lesli Harris, Council Member

The New Orleans City Council approved a 2027 general fund budget Thursday that reduced the anticipated deficit to $27 million — about 3.4% of the city’s general fund expenditures — from $96 million. 

The smaller deficit projection than September resulted primarily from new revenue measures and some spending cuts. 

Council Member Freddie King III said the city still needs to make an additional $20 million in cuts. 

Council Member Matthew Willard said, “We’re living within our means.”

According to the city charter the budget is balanced, said Council Member Eugene Green. 

Council Member and Budget Chair Lesli Harris said she was happy the budget restored money for a low-barrier homeless shelter that accommodates nearly 300 people every night.

The city was forced to deal with the budget gap because the Louisiana State Bond Commission wouldn’t approve operating expense borrowing, Council Member J.P. Morrill said. 

“From where we started to where we are now, we are in a much better place,” Mayor Helena Moreno told the council.

Next year won’t be any easier, Harris said. 

The city needs to implement a parcel fee for property owners who don’t pay taxes, said Council Member Aimee McCarron. These include churches and other nonprofits and government agencies. This will allow the city to expand the “pie” of property taxpayers to 100% from 60%, she said. 

The city plans to bring the measure before voters in 2027.  

Moreno said the city reduced general fund expenditures by moving $6.6 million from the general fund to special revenue funds or grant funds and cutting the city’s contingency fund by $19 million (leaving about $1 million). 

The city added $20 million in revenue from a partial millage roll forward, $1.95 million from increased permit fees, $1.78 million from increased emergency medical services collections, and $4.3 million in state short-term rental funding. Additionally, the city economist forecasts another $7.5 million in added revenue for the coming year and the city expects $3 million from a legal ruling.

In October the council approved a sanitation fee hike. 

The city’s fiscal year coincides with the calendar year. 

New Orleans last fall found itself unable to meet expenses for the remainder of the year due to overspending by the previous administration and delays in receipt of federal money. The State Bond Commission approved $125 million revenue anticipation notes, which were issued that fall and paid back earlier this year.  

The city planned to return to the bond commission in July for approval of $110 million of bonds for operating expenses but Moreno withdrew the request, saying she heard there was inadequate support on the Republican-dominated commission for the bonds. Moreno and all city council members are Democrats. 

New Orleans is rated Baa2 with a negative outlook by Moody’s Ratings, BBB-plus with a negative outlook by S&P Global Ratings and A-minus with a negative outlook by Fitch Ratings.

data.title: US signed off on sales of nearly 900,000 AI chips to China in six months, House committee says
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - The Trump administration approved shipments of nearly 900,000 advanced AI chips made by Nvidia and AMD for Chinese companies from December 2025 through May 2026, the House Foreign Affairs Committee said on Thursday. 

The approvals for 879,000 chip shipments by the Commerce Department included 75,000 for Alibaba ( BABA ), 150,000 for Tencent ( TCTZF ), 43,000 for Baidu ( BIDU ), and 4,000 for BYD, all on the Pentagon's list of alleged Chinese military-backed companies, the committee noted.

The unusual release of chip export licensing data comes as the administration of President Donald Trump faces heightened scrutiny following news about former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which has fueled renewed calls in Washington for a tougher stance on China.

Companies had sought permission to ship over 3.4 million chips to China during the period, the documents showed. It was not immediately clear how many of the approvals resulted in actual China-bound shipments of chips, which included Nvidia's ( NVDA ) H200 and AMD's equivalent MI325X.

News surrounding Huang has turned a spotlight on instances of Nvidia AI chips being smuggled to China that went unpunished, dialing up pressure on the Trump administration to crack down on Chinese tech ​threats.

"The fact that over 30% of the AI chips sent to China were shipped to companies that the Department of War has designated as Chinese military companies is astonishing, and calls into question whether Commerce conducted any serious national security review before approving these licenses," said Chris McGuire, a former US official and expert on the US-China technology battle.

Nvidia said in a statement that the approvals were "subject to strict conditions and limited volumes." It added that "despite receiving some licenses, we have since stopped shipping H200s to China."

AMD said it "complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations."

Alibaba ( BABA ), Tencent ( TCTZF ), Baidu ( BIDU ), BYD, the Commerce Department and the Chinese Embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

MOST DETAILED PUBLIC DISCLOSURE   

Former President Joe Biden had restricted Chinese access to the prized chips over fears that they would supercharge China's military and erode the US lead in artificial intelligence.

But Trump in December gave the green light for Nvidia to ship its H200 chip to China, rolling back Biden-era restrictions and drawing fierce criticism from China hawks across the US political spectrum.

Despite the approvals, questions swirled as to whether the AI chips were actually reaching Chinese shores.

In May, Reuters reported the US had cleared about 10 companies to buy the H200, but that no deliveries had taken place.

In testimony before the committee in July, Commerce Department official Jeffrey Kessler said shipments had begun but there had been 'very few.' Several major Chinese internet companies had each obtained about 10,000 H200 chips, Reuters has since reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

"This is the most detailed public disclosure in the history of the Export Control Reform Act," committee Chair Brian Mast, a Republican from Florida, said upon releasing the data, referring to 2018 legislation that expanded Commerce's authority to restrict the export of sensitive technologies for national security reasons.

(Reporting by Alexandra Alper, Ryan Patrick Jones, Katharine Jackson; Additional Reporting by David Shepardson; Editing by Scott Malone, Chris Sanders and Bill Berkrot)

WASHINGTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - The booming rollout of artificial intelligence technology could strain the US economy's capacity and further boost inflation that the Federal Reserve will have to counteract, Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said on Thursday, as AI firm Anthropic set a new record for an initial public offering of stock.

"The AI boom is contributing to the potential of overheating in the economy. I find it hard to ... look at that any other way," Goolsbee said in a conference call with reporters. "When you're getting major business investment, almost unprecedented levels of business investment, there's a high danger that the economy's capacity cannot handle that kind of a pig through the python."

Goolsbee said he sees the multitrillion-dollar pipeline of data-center projects already adding to what he referred to as "borderline, disturbingly high inflation rates" that are well above the Fed's 2% target and potentially heading higher.

He said he felt the Anthropic IPO, giving the company's early shareholders the ability to tap equity holdings well in excess of $1 trillion, could on its own become relevant to the path of the broader economy.

"A $1.5 trillion IPO. The question of what people are going to do with the money now that they have some access to that liquidity is going to become a macro-relevant statistic," Goolsbee said. "We're watching that."

DATA-CENTER BACKLASH

The US central bank is widely expected to raise interest rates by a quarter of a percentage point at its December 8-9 meeting. Fed policymakers also are wrestling with how the AI boom is influencing the economy.

The recent US midterm elections saw AI skepticism emerge at the polls, with municipalities in a number of states approving ballot initiatives that could limit how quickly and where data centers get built, potentially slowing the industry's breakneck evolution.

At the same time, the Fed this week held a high-level conference looking at the possible impact on productivity and the labor market should the new technologies diffuse through the economy and reach a potential that Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh has characterized as pivotal to US economic leadership.

In remarks at an earlier event on Thursday, Goolsbee said it was not yet clear what effect AI will have on productivity or the economy's underlying potential, noting that it took years - even decades - for other general-purpose technologies to change how businesses operated on a broad basis.

In the meantime, the Fed will have to cope with short-term effects that so far seem to be inflationary.

"The Fed's job is to prevent this thing from overheating the economy," with monetary policy set tight enough to keep demand and supply in balance, Goolsbee said at the event.

The Chicago Fed chief did not say if he would support a larger half-percentage-point rate hike at the December meeting, as at least one of his colleagues has advocated, but added that all options were on the table.

"The question of how steep the rate path is going to be and if there will be any rate increases should be determined, in my view, by whether you think inflation is going to be heading back to 2% on its own or not," Goolsbee said. "The evidence does not suggest we're on a path back to 2%."

(Reporting by Howard Schneider; Editing by Paul Simao)

data.title: TRADING DAY-World's biggest IPO? Pfft
data.description:
ORLANDO, Florida, Nov 19 (Reuters) - US stocks slumped 2% on Thursday, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq making fresh seven-month lows, as investors shrugged off the euphoria of Claude maker Anthropic's record-breaking market debut and focused instead on growing concerns over the longer-term outlook for the AI trade.

In my column today, I look at the respective economic hands held by Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping at the US-China summit today. Neither was particularly strong, and the ace in the pack for both leaders is AI. But reliance on AI may be their Achilles' heel.

Today's Key Reads

* Trump, Xi and Putin release 'peace declaration' from unprecedented summit

* Trump-Xi-Putin summit exposes Europe's power deficit: Bousso

* BOJ chief plays down soft consumption data, signals near-term rate hike

Nasdaq -2.3%, Dow -2.2%, S&P 500 -2% for longest losing streak since April 2024. * SECTORS/SHARES: All 11 sectors in the S&P 500 fall. Comms services, consumer cyclicals -3%. Tech, industrials, materials, healthcare -2%. Nvidia ( NVDA ) -3.3%, now -40% from peak last month. Williams-Sonoma -15%. Palo Alto Networks +6%. * FX: US dollar rises, dollar/yen nudges 160.00, Aussie dollar biggest G10 decliner. In EM, Colombian peso -1.5%, dollar/Brazil above 5.95. Euro zone yields up ~2 bps, US yields down 1-3 bps. * COMMODITIES/METALS: Copper slips to seven-month low, failing to bounce from yesterday's 6% slide. Oil rises ~0.5%. Gold slides again, -1.5% to $3,662/oz.

Today's Talking Points:

SomnambulANT

It was slashed by around a quarter from the expected valuation only a couple of months ago, but Anthropic's IPO still turned out to be the largest in history. The $83-a-share offer price raised $81 billion, putting the Claude maker's valuation at around $1.5 trillion. That briefly topped $2 trillion as shares changed hands at $115 in debut trading on Thursday. They closed at $97.

But longer-term doubts persist, chiefly around future revenues. Total compute commitments currently stand at around $900 billion, perhaps closer to $1 trillion. Around half of that is due by 2030. Assuming return on investment, operating margin, and tax, revenue needs to grow substantially. Analysis by the FT suggests Anthropic will need to be generating annual revenue of $600 billion, which is way more than Alphabet and Apple currently turn over. Last month, Anthropic's annualized revenue was running at just over $80 billion.

Soft landing? Not likely

The 2027 outlooks are flooding in, and for the US, the consensus - surprise, surprise! - is for another year of decent GDP growth and stock market gains. To be fair, there is a general recognition that the foundations for this rosy scenario are less sturdy than they were only a few months ago. That's due to inflation, a more hawkish Fed, and perhaps most importantly, worries that the AI trade correction morphs into something more serious. See above.

The US is increasingly reliant on AI, perhaps dangerously so. Apollo's Torsten Slok reckons AI is powering two-thirds of GDP growth, while Ajay Rajadhyaksha at Barclays says the consensus 15% EPS growth for next year would seal the strongest three-year stretch of earnings in "many decades". Dario Perkins at TS Lombard notes the parabolic surge in AI investment to a record share of GDP, and asks the simple question: "Have you ever seen a macro chart do this and it all turns out OK?"

Debt of latitude

If the consensus 2027 outlook for growth and stocks is relatively upbeat, the same can't be said for fiscal policy. According to JPMorgan's Joe Lupton and Maia Cook, fiscal policy in developed markets has become "disconnected" from the business cycle. Despite the strong post-pandemic recovery and unemployment near 50-year lows, developed economy deficits this year are projected to be 5.5% of GDP, the highest outside a recession since at least World War Two. More than 70% of developed economies have weaker fiscal balances than before the pandemic.

Hopes that this can be fixed by inflation, growth, or a combination of the two, are fading. Bigger debt burdens, aging populations, rising welfare costs, and rising interest rates are a toxic mix. Developed economies need roughly a 4.6 pp improvement in the primary balance just to stabilize debt, Lupton and Cook argue, and "substantially" larger adjustments to get debt back to pre-pandemic ratios. The US, France, and the UK stand out. Buckle up.

data.title: Gap cuts forecast, but signs of Old Navy recovery lift shares
data.description:
By Neil J Kanatt and Danielle Kaye

Nov 19 (Reuters) - Gap cut its annual sales and profit forecasts on Thursday after a slower-than-expected start to the holiday quarter, even as improving trends at Old Navy, its largest brand, signaled its turnaround efforts were gaining traction.

Shares of the US apparel retailer rose more than 2% in extended trading after Old Navy posted better-than-expected quarterly sales and the company named Vuori executive Ashley Kechter to lead Athleta, its struggling activewear brand.

Investors have been seeking signs that Old Navy is recovering from a recent slump. While the namesake Gap brand has driven recent growth, the rest of Gap's portfolio - encompassing Old Navy, Athleta and Banana Republic - has lagged.

Gap earlier this year blamed weak sales of dresses and other seasonal categories on merchandising missteps at Old Navy and appointed retail veteran Michael Francis as the banner's chief executive in August.

Old Navy's revenue rose 1% to $2.30 billion in the third quarter, beating analysts' expectations. Gap Chief Executive Richard Dickson said in a statement the banner showed "meaningful sequential improvement."

Gap now expects fiscal 2026 sales to be roughly flat, compared with its previous forecast for growth of 1% to 1.5%. Analysts on average had expected growth of 1.4%, according to data compiled by LSEG.

The company lowered its adjusted annual earnings forecast to between $2.29 and $2.34 per share from its prior range of $2.35 to $2.45.

Athleta, Gap's smallest banner by revenue, continues to face pressure as it works through excess inventory and seeks to boost brand desirability. It reported a 15% drop in comparable sales in the third quarter.

For the holiday quarter, the retailer expects sales to range from flat to down 1%, compared with analysts' expectations for a 2.6% increase. The company said the current quarter started slowly before improving in recent weeks.

TJX said this week that holiday demand for discounted merchandise remained strong, but Target ( TGT ) reported continued weakness in apparel, particularly in women's fashion.

For the third quarter ended October 31, Gap reported net sales of $4.01 billion, compared with analysts' average estimate of about $4.02 billion, while adjusted earnings per share of 82 cents beat expectations of 78 cents.

(Reporting by Neil J Kanatt in Bengaluru and Danielle Kaye in Los Angeles; Editing by Tasim Zahid)

data.title: Bausch + Lomb's eye-drop drug fails to reduce pain after laser surgery in trial
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Bausch + Lomb ( BLCO ) said on Thursday its experimental eye-drop treatment failed to show a significant reduction in pain over the first 24 hours after laser eye surgery in a mid-stage study.

However, the drug showed signs of benefit in secondary and exploratory analyses, including greater pain relief shortly after surgery and faster corneal healing.

The contact lens maker said it plans to discuss the results with the US Food and Drug Administration as it considers next steps for the drug, including a potential late-stage trial.

Here are some details:

* The mid-stage trial tested two doses of BL1332 in 129 patients undergoing photorefractive keratectomy, or PRK, a laser procedure used to correct vision

* US-listed shares of the eye-care company were down 1.4% in extended trading

* Ocular surface pain is a common complication of eye surgery and certain eye diseases, and there are currently no approved treatments that directly target its underlying nerve pathways, the company said

* At six hours after surgery, secondary goal of complete pain relief was reported by 14% and 14.6% of patients receiving the two BL1332 doses, compared with 3.7% of patients receiving placebo

* The company also said patients treated with BL1332 showed signs of faster healing of the cornea, the eye's outer surface

(Reporting by Siddhi Mahatole in Bengaluru; Editing by Tasim Zahid and Shinjini Ganguli)
