data.title: GLOBAL MARKETS-Stocks fall as Anthropic debut fails to ease AI concerns; dollar rises
data.description:
(Updates to US stock market close)

* Dollar index ticks up, Latam currencies slide

* Oil prices rise on Hormuz attacks concern

* Anthropic rises 17% in stock market debut

By Rodrigo Campos

NEW YORK/LONDON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Global stocks fell on Thursday with sliding tech shares as Anthropic's debut failed to allay investor concerns about AI returns, while oil prices rose as attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz grabbed market attention.

Investors have said that Anthropic's market reception over the coming days and weeks will be heavily scrutinized to gauge broader sentiment toward investments in artificial intelligence. The Claude developer's initial public offering was priced at $83 a share, valuing Anthropic at about $1.5 trillion before the stock rose as much as 39% to trade at $115.10.

"Investors are making changes in their portfolio to incorporate Anthropic, so I wouldn't extrapolate a whole lot of meaning from (Thursday's) trading behavior, whether it's up or down," said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital in St. Louis.

Ellerbroek pointed to a leadership change in chipmaker Nvidia ( NVDA ) and to shrinking bets on the growth in data center capex as having an impact on investors.

"Data centers are going to be more expensive to build and they're going to be built more slowly," Ellerbroek said.

Anthropic's stock closed up 17% on its debut, valuing the company at just below $1.8 trillion.

"We can't underestimate the importance of this IPO. It sort of serves as a valuation for the wider AI ecosystem," said Fiona Cincotta, senior market analyst at StoneX.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1,101.11 points, or 2.19%, to 49,097.06, the S&P 500 fell 147.80 points, or 2.02%, to 7,175.83 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 550.68 points, or 2.25%, to 23,879.20.

MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe fell 17.76 points, or 1.65%, to 1,056.80. The pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 0.88%, while emerging market stocks fell 18.79 points, or 1.27%, to 1,465.49.

DOLLAR AND OIL EDGE HIGHER

The dollar ticked up against developed peers but some sensitive currencies sold off on concerns about tightening financial conditions. Mexico's peso fell 1.4% and Colombia's peso dropped 1.8%.

"We're seeing a scramble for US dollar liquidity, and the entire emerging market complex is suffering a severe selloff as global financial conditions tighten," said Karl Schamotta, chief market strategist at Corpay.

"With sentiment on the US technology sector showing signs of crumbling while expectations for the Fed's policy path climb, stress is rising in the currencies most exposed to a slowdown in the AI buildout," Schamotta said.

Against a basket of peers, the greenback has climbed to 19-month highs on the back of expectations of tighter monetary policy out of Washington. On Thursday, the dollar index rose for an eighth consecutive session and was up 0.14% to 103.96.

In commodities, oil prices settled flat on the day but were higher late as earlier reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz more than offset rising US crude inventories and forecasts for a global oil surplus.

Iran's navy said in a statement carried by state media that two oil tankers hit naval mines in the waterway and "exploded" on Thursday. Reuters could not independently verify the report.

US crude rose 0.66% to $83.81 a barrel and Brent rose to $92.72 per barrel, up 0.84% on the day.

Spot gold fell 2.54% to $3,627.55 an ounce, and spot silver fell 4.36% to $43.04 an ounce. Copper declined 0.14% to $12,453.00 a ton.

(Reporting by Rodrigo Campos, Marc Jones, Saqib Iqbal Ahmed, Seher Dareen, Medha Singh, Utkarsh Hathi and Ragini Mathur; Editing by Kevin Liffey, Hugh Lawson, Nick Zieminski, Will Dunham and Alexander Smith)

data.title: Energy Transfer Completes Acquisition of Vaquero Midstream
data.description:
DALLAS--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Energy Transfer LP (TXSE: ET) has completed its previously announced acquisition of Vaquero Midstream LLC. Total consideration for the transaction was $1.95 billion in cash and approximately 33.3 million newly issued Energy Transfer common units.

The acquired assets add the Caymus Processing Complex, which includes three processing trains with a total capacity of approximately 675 MMcf/d and approximately 300 miles of pipeline serving leading operators across some of the most active areas of the Delaware Basin.

The transaction is expected to further strengthen Energy Transfer's Permian footprint by increasing access to growing natural gas and NGL production volumes while enhancing connectivity to the Partnership's broader midstream platform.

Energy Transfer LP (TXSE: ET) owns and operates one of the largest and most diversified portfolios of energy assets in the United States, with approximately 140,000 miles of pipeline and associated energy infrastructure. Energy Transfer’s strategic network spans 44 states with assets in all of the major U.S. production basins. Energy Transfer is a publicly traded limited partnership with core operations that include complementary natural gas midstream, intrastate and interstate transportation and storage assets; crude oil, natural gas liquids (“NGL”) and refined product transportation and terminalling assets; and NGL fractionation. Energy Transfer also owns the general partner interests, the incentive distribution rights and approximately 28 million common units (representing 15% of the aggregate outstanding common units and Class D units) of Sunoco LP (TXSE: SUN), the managing member interests in SunocoCorp LLC (TXSE: SUNC), and the general partner interests and approximately 46 million common units (representing 32% of the outstanding common units) of USA Compression Partners, LP (TXSE: USAC). For more information, visit the Energy Transfer LP website at www.energytransfer.com.

Sunoco LP (TXSE: SUN) is a leading energy infrastructure and fuel distribution master limited partnership operating across 33 countries and territories in North America, the Greater Caribbean, and Europe. SUN's midstream operations include an extensive network of approximately 14,000 miles of pipeline and over 170 terminals. This critical infrastructure complements SUN's fuel distribution operations which distribute over 17 billion gallons annually to approximately 11,000 Sunoco and partner-branded retail locations, as well as independent dealers and commercial customers. SUN's general partner is owned by Energy Transfer LP. For more information, visit the Sunoco LP website at www.sunocolp.com.

SunocoCorp LLC (TXSE: SUNC) is a publicly traded limited liability company that owns a direct limited partner interest in Sunoco LP. For more information, visit the Sunoco LP website at www.sunocolp.com.

USA Compression Partners, LP (TXSE: USAC) is one of the nation’s largest independent providers of natural gas compression services in terms of total compression fleet horsepower. USAC partners with a broad customer base composed of producers, processors, gatherers, and transporters of natural gas and crude oil. The move came in a session where the major U.S. indexes spent the afternoon sharply lower as Anthropic PBC made its Nasdaq debut. ( OKTA ) , Cloudflare, Inc. ( NET ) .

Why the Sector Is Moving

Reuters described AI as reshaping the cyber arms race, helping attackers find and exploit vulnerabilities faster while increasing demand for software that can identify, block and respond to threats. data.title: ROHM Develops TP-PFC Controller IC for GaN High-Frequency Switching
data.description:
Santa Clara, CA and Kyoto, Japan, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- ROHM Semiconductor today announced it has developed the BM85060FV, a totem-pole power factor correction (TP-PFC) controller IC for high-efficiency, compact AC-DC power supplies. A key feature is its ability to operate in the MHz band, supporting high-frequency switching with GaN HEMTs.

As consumer electronics and industrial equipment become more sophisticated, they require more power while also demanding smaller size and higher efficiency. Stricter energy regulations further drive the need for both improved operating efficiency and lower no-load power consumption. GaN HEMTs are gaining adoption due to their high-frequency switching performance.

Additionally, when paired with a bridgeless TP-PFC controller such as BM85060FV, system designers can significantly reduce power loss and solution footprint, enabling compact, high-efficiency power supplies. However, conventional MCU-based TP-PFC control has posed challenges in terms of power consumption, circuit size, cost, and achieving high-frequency switching with GaN HEMTs.

This new product enables a system-level efficiency of 99% in 300 to 500 W-class AC-DC power supplies. The high switching frequency allows for the miniaturization of peripheral components, resulting in a smaller solution footprint.

No-load current consumption of 150 μA - a 70%* reduction compared to standard products - makes it easier to reduce system standby power consumption and contributes to the development of power supply systems that meet the energy-saving requirements of DOE Level 7 and CoC Tier 2.

Furthermore, the device incorporates various protection functions required for AC-DC power supplies, including a lightning surge protection circuit, which helps reduce the design burden and improve system reliability.

Sales of the new product began in November 2026. Online sales have also started, and it is available for purchase through online distributors such as DigiKey, Mouser and Farnell. Additionally, a 330W output TP-PFC evaluation board featuring the “BM85060FV” is available to support the development of high-efficiency AC-DC power supplies utilizing GaN HEMTs.

ROHM will continue to contribute to the further miniaturization and power efficiency of electronic devices by providing power solutions that combine power semiconductors - including GaN HEMTs - with analog ICs designed to maximize their performance.

Application Examples
• AC adapters
• Consumer electronics such as projectors
• Compact industrial equipment
Ideal for high-efficiency, compact 300–500 W-class AC-DC power supplies.

data.title: John Forsyth, Cirrus Logic President and CEO, Elected Chair of Semiconductor Industry Association
data.description:
SAN JOSE, Calif., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA) today announced that Cirrus Logic ( CRUS ) President and CEO John Forsyth has been elected Chair of the SIA Board of Directors. Tom Caulfield, Executive Chairman of GlobalFoundries ( GFS ) , was elected Vice Chair. AMD Chair and CEO Lisa Su, who served as 2026 Chair, will continue to serve on the Board and the Leadership Committee. SIA, the voice of the semiconductor industry, represents 99% of the U.S. semiconductor industry by revenue and nearly two-thirds of non-U.S. chip firms.

"Congratulations to John Forsyth on his election as SIA Chair. John has been a trusted partner since my first day at SIA, and he brings steady, strategic judgment to a pivotal year for our industry," said SIA President and CEO Michael Robbins. "With a new Congress, SIA's 50th anniversary, and the work of extending the Advanced Manufacturing Investment Credit ahead of us, I look forward to working with John, Tom Caulfield, and our entire Board to strengthen America's semiconductor leadership. I also want to thank Lisa Su for an outstanding year as our Chair. Her steadfast leadership strengthens SIA and our industry, and I am tremendously grateful for her guidance and counsel."

Forsyth brings more than 20 years of experience in semiconductor industry leadership. As president and CEO of Cirrus Logic ( CRUS ), he leads the company in developing high-precision, low-power audio and mixed-signal semiconductor solutions for a broad range of consumer, automotive, and industrial applications. Forsyth has served as president and chief executive officer of Cirrus Logic ( CRUS ) since January 2021. He joined the company in 2014 through its acquisition of Wolfson Microelectronics and was named president in 2020 after previous roles including chief strategy officer and vice president of marketing.

"I'm honored to serve as SIA Chair at such an important time for our industry," said John Forsyth, president and CEO of Cirrus Logic ( CRUS ). "America's leadership in the next wave of semiconductor innovation depends on both a thriving domestic industry and close collaboration between that industry and government. I look forward to working with SIA's Board of Directors and members to strengthen that collaboration, accelerate the build-out of a more resilient domestic supply chain, and keep the U.S. at the forefront of this critical technology."

About SIA
The Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA) is the voice of the semiconductor industry, one of America's top export industries and a key driver of America's economic strength, national security, and global competitiveness. SIA represents 99% of the U.S. semiconductor industry by revenue and nearly two-thirds of non-U.S. chip firms. Through this coalition, SIA seeks to strengthen leadership of semiconductor manufacturing, design, and research by working with Congress, the Administration, and key industry stakeholders around the world to encourage policies that fuel innovation, propel business, and drive international competition. data.title: Curtiss-Wright Expands 2026 Buyback Program by $250 Million, Maintains Dividend

04:57 PM EST, 11/19/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Curtiss-Wright ( CW ) expanded its 2026 share repurchase program by $250 million, it said Thursday.

The program will be conducted in concurrence with the existing $60 million share buyback plan, the company said.

Also, the board authorized $60 million in repurchases beginning in January 2027 via a 10b5-1 program, according to the company. Curtiss-Wright ( CW ) will have $290 million in remaining open authorization entering 2027, it said.

The company maintained its quarterly dividend at $0.26 per share, payable Dec. 11 to stockholders of record Nov. 27.
